title: MTIA 300: Meta’s First Training Chip Featuring Built-in NICs and Collective Offloading Engines
evidence_span: Sections II and IV describe integrated RDMA NIC chiplets, dedicated message engines, near-memory reductions, and HCCL software. Section V.D.1 reports 3.9x communication performance versus H100 for a roughly 150B-parameter DLRM using 40 accelerators and local batch 6144. Table IV reports normalized Perf/TCO separately. Section V.B reports an H100/NCCL advantage for small messages; Section VI discusses numerical, datatype, runtime, and training-batch limitations.
problem: Recommendation-model training is communication-bound because embedding tables contain most model parameters and hybrid parallelism generates frequent AllReduce, AllToAll, and AllGather operations that compete with computation on GPU resources.
method_or_artifact: MTIA 300 co-designs compute, integrated network chiplets, dedicated message engines, near-memory collective reduction, and the HCCL communication library; collectives are compiled into autonomous dependency graphs rather than launched as compute-grid kernels.
workload_or_benchmark: DLRM of approximately 150B parameters implemented with TorchRec/TorchInductor and distributed Shampoo. Communication comparison: 40 MTIA 300 versus 40 H100, local batch 6144. Overlap microbenchmark: 1000 TF32 4K x 4K x 4K GEMMs with collectives across 16 accelerators.
hardware_or_process_assumptions: Table I: 1.9 GHz, 216 GB HBM3E, 912 W TDP (667 W typical), compute chiplet 25.6 x 31.4 mm, two network chiplets each 25.6 x 9.3 mm. Section II: 12 x 800 Gbps RDMA NICs and 16 message engines. Process node not established in extracted sections; TDP is not measured workload energy.
baselines: H100 with NCCL for collective operations; TorchRec/TorchInductor on both platforms for the production DLRM
Table IV reference: 40 H100 accelerators at local batch 6144, normalized Perf/TCO 1.00
metrics: 3.9x communication performance relative to H100: 40 accelerators, local batch 6144, approximately 150B-parameter DLRM (V.D.1)
Normalized Perf/TCO 1.39 for 40 MTIA 300 at local batch 6144 versus 1.00 for 40 H100 at the same batch (Table IV)
Normalized Perf/TCO 1.42 for 24 MTIA 300 at local batch 10240 versus the Table IV H100 reference; global batch held constant
limits: Author-reported evaluation, not independent replication. Communication speedup and Perf/TCO are distinct; neither establishes universal end-to-end speedup. Cost-accounting inputs and amortization assumptions were not found in the extracted evaluation and remain unresolved. Small-message collectives favor H100/NCCL; compute-heavy workloads, numerical parity, unsupported datatypes, eager overhead, and convergence/batch tradeoffs limit generality. Exact article-only 940 GB/s and less-than-0.5% figures remain supplemental, not paper-verified metrics.

supplemental_sources.limits: Article-only exact figures such as 940 GB/s and less than 0.5% are not promoted into the paper-derived metric list.
